reading.body:
CoreSite AT1 sits in downtown Atlanta at 55 Marietta Street, occupying 62,000 square feet of technical space. No IT load figure in megawatts is published on the operator's spec page, so no power-to-rack or power-to-accelerator translation is possible here. The floor area alone cannot drive a reliable power estimate without a watts-per-square-foot assumption the operator has not supplied, so the campus's raw compute capacity remains unquantifiable from published data.

The six certifications qualify AT1 to host workloads under financial audit controls, payment card security standards, healthcare privacy rules, and federal information security frameworks. SOC 1 Type 2 and SOC 2 Type 2 address financial and operational controls respectively. PCI DSS and HIPAA open the facility to regulated payment and health data. ISO 27001 and NIST 800-53 satisfy customers requiring internationally recognized or US government-aligned security baselines. None of these certifications are specific to AI training or inference, but they do not preclude it, and regulated industries increasingly run AI workloads inside exactly these compliance envelopes.

Georgia has 33 mapped facilities in this site's dataset, but only 2 of those publish a megawatt figure, totaling 42 MW across the state. AT1 ranks third by published megawatts in the state, yet because AT1 itself publishes no megawatt figure, that ranking reflects the ordering logic of the dataset rather than a confirmed power position. The 42 MW total covers only the two facilities that disclosed numbers, meaning the true installed capacity across Georgia's 33 mapped sites is unknown. AT1's significance to AI in this market cannot be confirmed or ruled out from what the operator has chosen to publish.
